user.title: Choose the thermostat
user.description: Select the Versatile Thermostat to apply device quirks to. Only thermostats compatible with at least one quirk are listed.

quirk.title: Quirk of the underlying

entities.title: Entities of the quirk {quirk}
entities.description: Check the entities of the device {underlying}. They are prefilled from the device. On ZHA, the valve entities are disabled by default: enable them first.

data_description.heating_position: Zigbee2MQTT: heating_valve_position. ZHA: Valve opening degree. It must be the opening degree entity of the thermostat.
data_description.idle_position: Zigbee2MQTT: idle_valve_position. ZHA: Valve closing degree. On this device it is the idle opening, not a closing degree.
data_description.external_temperature: Zigbee2MQTT: external_temperature_input. ZHA: External temperature sensor value.
data_description.sensor_select: Zigbee2MQTT: the temperature sensor select. ZHA: the External temperature sensor switch.
data_description.adaptive_control: Only used to report a setting that prevents the quirk from working.
data_description.open_window: Only used to report a setting that prevents the quirk from working.
data_description.opening_degree: Zigbee2MQTT: valve_opening_degree. ZHA: Valve opening degree. It must be the opening degree entity of the thermostat.
data_description.closing_degree: Zigbee2MQTT: valve_closing_degree. ZHA: Valve closing degree. The quirk writes it: do not configure it in the thermostat.
data_description.trv_mode: Zigbee2MQTT: trv_mode. The quirk keeps it on 1 with the direct valve control, on 2 otherwise.
data_description.valve_position: Zigbee2MQTT: valve_position. With the direct valve control it must be the opening degree entity of the thermostat.

data.keep_schedule: Keep the schedule of the TRV

data_description.temperature_source: Temperature source restored after the kick. Use Remote only if another automation feeds the external temperature: its last value is then restored.
data_description.delta: Gap between the TRV setpoint and the fake temperature. Must be higher than the TRV temperature accuracy.
data_description.pulse_delay: Time to let the TRV react before restoring the temperature sensor.
data_description.hot_step: After the cold step, also send a fake temperature above the setpoint to force an idle transition. Enable only if the valve does not reach the requested opening without it.
data_description.keep_schedule: Accept the schedule preset of the TRV (auto) when the thermostat heats. The other presets are always corrected.
data_description.legacy_converter: Enable it if your Zigbee2MQTT converter is old: it shows the preset manual as the mode auto. The mode heat is then sent as auto, auto is read as heat, and heat (valve forced open) is not supported.
data_description.restore_setpoint: When the TRV is taken off its schedule, write the setpoint of the thermostat again if the schedule changed it.
data_description.pre_open: When the thermostat closes the valve, open it to this value first so that the motor closes it fully. 0 disables it.
data_description.slam_delay: Time the valve stays at the pre-opening before it is closed.

abort.already_configured: A quirks entry already exists for this thermostat. Use its options to change it.
abort.no_vtherm: No Versatile Thermostat without quirks is compatible with an available quirk. A quirk needs for example an over_climate thermostat with direct valve control.
abort.no_quirk_selected: No quirk was selected. Delete the entry if you do not need it anymore.

abort.vtherm_not_found: The Versatile Thermostat of this entry was not found.

hooks_unavailable.title: Versatile Thermostat Quirks cannot start
hooks_unavailable.description: The installed vtherm_api does not provide the underlying hooks. Update Versatile Thermostat (vtherm_api 0.9.0 or later is required), then restart Home Assistant.

unknown_quirk.title: Unknown quirk
unknown_quirk.description: The quirk {quirk} configured for {underlying} of {name} does not exist in this version of the plugin. It is ignored. Reconfigure or delete the entry.

incompatible_quirk.title: Incompatible quirk
incompatible_quirk.description: The quirk {quirk} configured for {underlying} is not compatible with the configuration of {name} (type of thermostat or valve control). It is ignored.

sync_device_internal_temp.title: Device temperature synchronization enabled
sync_device_internal_temp.description: {name}: the quirk {quirk} on {underlying} needs the device temperature synchronization disabled in the thermostat, because it uses the external temperature of the device.

closing_entity_configured.title: Closing degree entity configured
closing_entity_configured.description: {name}: {entity} is configured as closing degree entity. With the quirk {quirk} on {underlying}, remove it: the quirk manages this entity itself.

opening_entity_mismatch.title: Opening degree entity mismatch
opening_entity_mismatch.description: {name}: the opening degree entity is {entity} but the quirk {quirk} on {underlying} expects {expected}.

entity_disabled.title: Entity disabled
entity_disabled.description: {name}: the entity {entity} needed by the quirk {quirk} on {underlying} is disabled. Enable it in the entity settings.

adaptive_control_enabled.title: Adaptive temperature control enabled
adaptive_control_enabled.description: {name}: {entity} is on. Turn it off on the device, otherwise the quirk {quirk} on {underlying} cannot move the valve.

open_window_enabled.title: Open window detection enabled
open_window_enabled.description: {name}: {entity} is on. Turn it off on the device, otherwise the quirk {quirk} on {underlying} may be disturbed.

preset_keeps_changing.title: Radiator valve preset keeps changing
preset_keeps_changing.description: {name}: the quirk {quirk} cannot keep {underlying} in the preset {preset}, it is now {current}. The quirk stopped correcting it after 3 attempts. Check what changes the preset (the device, an automation, another integration). The quirk starts again when the thermostat changes mode.

outdated_converter.title: Zigbee2MQTT converter too old
outdated_converter.description: {name}: {underlying} shows the state auto while its preset is manual, so the converter of Zigbee2MQTT for this valve is out of date. Update Zigbee2MQTT, or enable the option Legacy Zigbee2MQTT converter of the quirk {quirk}, which translates the mode for the thermostat. Until then the thermostat reads the wrong mode.

closing_degree_keeps_changing.title: Valve closing degree keeps changing
closing_degree_keeps_changing.description: {name}: the quirk {quirk} cannot keep {entity} at {expected}, it is now {current}. The quirk stopped correcting it after 3 attempts. Check what changes it (an automation, another integration). The quirk starts again when the thermostat changes mode.

follow_underlying_enabled.title: Following of the underlying setpoint enabled
follow_underlying_enabled.description: {name}: the thermostat follows the setpoint changes of {underlying}. With the quirk {quirk}, a setpoint written by the schedule of the TRV can then be taken as a user change. Disable "Follow underlying temperature changes" in the thermostat.

trv_mode_keeps_changing.title: TRV mode keeps changing
trv_mode_keeps_changing.description: {name}: the quirk {quirk} cannot keep the TRV mode of {underlying} on {mode}, it is now {current}. The quirk stopped correcting it after 3 attempts in an hour. Check what changes it. The quirk starts again when the thermostat leaves OFF.

valve_scale_percent.title: Valve opening scale in percent
valve_scale_percent.description: {name}: {entity} goes up to {max} but the thermostat drives it in percent, so the valve of {underlying} never opens fully. Empty the max opening degrees of the thermostat (or set it to {max}).

closing_entity_not_supported.title: Closing degree entity not supported
closing_entity_not_supported.description: {name}: {entity} is configured as closing degree entity, but {underlying} has none (quirk {quirk}). Remove it from the thermostat.
